clue.text: Passes over the Guardian's standard

indicators.note: in a down-free across clue, over means the first piece sits ahead of the next

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass, the dip between two peaks
the newspaper speaking of itself: the Guardian's is ours

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor waving through something that meets the paper's house standard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the paper that printed this clue, so 'the Guardian's' is 'ours' from the setter's side.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colours are its flag, a standard carried into battle or on parade.

clue.text: Church gathered to welcome new material

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: people who gathered met together

explanation.surface: A congregation gathered to welcome a fresh hymn book or sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is a building substance used to bind bricks and stone.

clue.text: Slight problem with some fixtures and fittings

indicators.note: a problem with the word Slight means its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A minor issue found during a house sale with what's included.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps are among the items fitted in a home that a buyer may or may not inherit.

clue.text: Posh trend — pace about bare floorboards?

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smart interior design fashion: walk across exposed wooden floors.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the old 'U and non-U' distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Floorboards without any rug or covering describe a room with no carpet laid.

clue.text: A relative getting up with cereal, ultimately for fibre

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word cereal

parts.note: last letter of cereal

explanation.surface: A relative rising and having breakfast cereal for the roughage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff natural strand from an agave plant, used for rope.

clue.text: Musician — one deliberately getting the count wrong?

definitions.text: one deliberately getting the count wrong?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who fiddles figures, falsifying accounts on purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the slang verb 'fiddle', to cheat with the books; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a violinist and a cheat who falsifies accounts or tallies.

clue.text: Amazing soft drinks, Tango I see

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange, so several are Fantas
T is Tango in the NATO alphabet
said aloud, I see sounds like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: Enthusing about a fizzy drink, with Tango, another British orange pop, in view.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British orange soft drink, misdirecting toward a drinks list, but here it is just the NATO letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extraordinary or incredible.

clue.text: Hell's cold: it's round and flat

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, and Dante's infernal city
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A claim that hell is chilly, oddly followed by a remark about shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat circular object, such as a plate or record, has this shape.

clue.text: Title of cricket ground's cool

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A remark that the title of a cricket ground sounds rather trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's, in north-west London, is the home of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Your Lordship' is a form of address for a peer or judge, a rank of honour.

clue.text: Contemplates Mirror and Sun

parts.note: a mirror reflects light
S is the abbreviation for Sunday, the Sun's day

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up two British tabloid newspapers, the Mirror and the Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make these look like the two tabloids, but they are just a verb and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To think deeply or ponder is to mull something over.

clue.text: Wonderful! First Macbeth, then Hamlet briefly, making a comeback?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the play title is all that is taken

parts.note: first letter of Macbeth

indicators.note: coming back means the shortened word is written backwards
cut short, so the last letter of the cigar is dropped

parts.note: Hamlet is a well-known British brand of small cigar

explanation.surface: A theatre programme of Shakespeare tragedies, Macbeth then a returning Hamlet, hailed as wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is not the play here but a brand of cigar famous from British TV adverts; CIGA reversed gives AGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, 'magic!' is British slang for brilliant or terrific.

clue.text: Type of soldiers covering partners with return fire

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters wrap around and cover the partners

parts.note: the SAS is the British special forces regiment
North and South are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: returning means the word fire is read backwards

explanation.surface: Special forces giving covering fire to their comrades and shooting back.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South are partners in the card game bridge, a crossword staple for 'partners'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sans serif is a typeface without the small strokes at the ends of letters.

clue.text: Born to talk banally about methane, say

parts.note: a born leader is a natural one
to gas is to chatter idly at length

explanation.surface: Someone apparently destined from birth to drone on about methane.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of the fuel piped from underground deposits to homes.

clue.text: Man perhaps spreading lies

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters of lies into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who perhaps goes about spreading falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Perhaps China's promise to take liberal prisoner with Queen

indicators.note: taking in a letter means it goes inside the word

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
POW is a prisoner of war
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A statement about whether China will free a liberal dissident held alongside the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: China is an example of a dominant nation with global influence.

clue.text: Hotel worker is nice to pert model

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Advice that a hotel employee should be polite to a cheeky fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: The person at a hotel's front desk who greets guests and checks them in.

clue.text: Criminal bears arms? Shame

indicators.note: a criminal version of the words is a corrupted, rearranged one

explanation.surface: An outlaw carries weapons, to everyone's disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To humiliate someone or make them feel awkward.

clue.text: Mammal to help out after bearing insect

indicators.note: the reworked word follows the bearing letter

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: out means the letters of help are in disarray

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A large animal steps in to assist after carrying a small bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest living land animal, with a trunk and tusks.

clue.text: Skip American politician being caught by cleaner

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a duster is a cloth for cleaning
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An American politician skipping out before being caught by the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British word for a large open rubbish container, which Americans call by this brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US, the big metal bin for builders' rubbish goes by this name.

clue.text: Neural defect has bachelor telephone dead actress

indicators.note: a defect makes the word neural go wrong, rearranging its letters

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
to telephone someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A medical report: a nerve disorder, a bachelor, a phone call, and a deceased performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was an American film star, the late screen partner and wife of Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Discontented poor Indian and commonplace — not like him!

definitions.text: Discontented poor Indian and commonplace — not like him!

indicators.note: with their contents removed, each word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A royal who is set apart from the unhappy, the poor and the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: PR, IN and CE come from the three emptied words; the whole clue then describes a royal, who is nothing like them.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's son lives in privilege, unlike the poor or the ordinary.

clue.text: Remained utterly sober

indicators.note: utterly is read as 'when uttered', spoken aloud

parts.note: staid means sober and serious

explanation.surface: Someone who kept completely dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like 'completely' but means spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed and remained both mean continued in the same place.

clue.text: Bishop's pawn has work with English opening

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word English is used

parts.note: first letter of English

explanation.surface: A chess game: the bishop's pawn moves while the player uses the English Opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface hides that 'Bishop' is the definition; the English Opening is a real chess opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Catholic Church holds office as Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Nonconformist getting whisky on the house?

parts.note: something on the house costs nothing, paid by the bar
whisky is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: A rebel happily accepting a complimentary whisky at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives by their own rules rather than society's is an independent soul.

clue.text: Consume tea brewed at university

indicators.note: brewing stirs the letters of tea into a new order

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university, as at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student drinking tea made in college.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish all the food on one's plate is to eat it entirely.

clue.text: Fuel cell's casing holds ordinary acid, primarily

indicators.note: holding means the outer letters contain the others
the casing is the outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word cell

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word acid

parts.note: first letter of acid

explanation.surface: A battery's shell contains ordinary acid as its main fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a fossil fuel burned for heat and power.

clue.text: One on Saturn trip, taking in ring and comet's tail?

definitions.text: One on Saturn trip, taking in ring and comet's tail?

indicators.note: the single letter sits on, ahead of, the scrambled part

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word comet, whose tail is its last letter

explanation.surface: A space traveller on a voyage to Saturn, passing its rings and a comet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saturn trip' reads as a voyage, but trip rearranges SATURN with O to give STRONAU; the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller might journey toward Saturn and pass rings and comets on the way.

clue.text: Weather to turn rainy in the end

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a key or handle

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word rainy is taken

parts.note: last letter of rainy

explanation.surface: A forecast that conditions will eventually turn wet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective describing weather with strong gusts.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery conditions with lots of moving air describe a kind of weather.

clue.text: Trunks almost all removed — smashing result for swimmers

indicators.note: nearly every letter of trunks is taken away, leaving only its first

parts.note: first letter of Trunks

indicators.note: smashing breaks up the letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose trunks nearly came off, a smashing result for the other bathers.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the one letter left of Trunks, comes first, then RESULT is rearranged as URTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea turtles are reptiles that swim the oceans.

clue.text: For each side upon tumbling meteor

indicators.note: the first piece sits upon, ahead of, the second

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: tumbling sends the letters of side into a new order

explanation.surface: Something falling from space, tumbling on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Perseids are an annual August shower of shooting stars.
